title: The Cover of the Free Port
premise: Ansel Vasquez, a financial-crimes investigator who launders her own grief by working unattributable cases, receives calls on a burner phone from her sister Marisol — who died two years ago in the 'accidental' fire at the Meridian Free Port. The voice is real, and it belongs to a woman who faked her death to infiltrate the port's custodial syndicate, which is preparing to destroy a warehouse of seized evidence as an insured 'accident' that will also kill the only witness to their founding crime. Ansel must trace the money behind the fire that nearly killed Marisol, expose the syndicate before the staged disaster, and decide whether justice served outside the law can ever be handed down cleanly. In the end, Marisol survives by staying dead, the syndicate falls through Ansel's quietly planted ledger, and Ansel inherits not wealth but the burden of remembering what official records will erase.
about_author: Paloma Quintana spent a decade auditing shipping manifests in Caribbean free ports before turning to fiction, and she still keeps a burner phone charged out of habit. She writes thrillers about people who do the right thing in ways no court would recognize.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She closes another unattributable case for a law firm that pays her to make scandals disappear into paperwork, establishing her moral exhaustion and skill. A package arrives containing a burner phone with no sender. That night it rings: Marisol's voice says her name. Emotional beat: numb competence cracked open by the impossible.

chapters.title: The Voice That Drowned
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, intercut with Marisol's. Ansel verifies the voice against old voicemails while Marisol, alive under a new identity inside the Meridian Free Port, makes a desperate call she shouldn't. They agree on one contact rule and one meeting place. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into suspicion — is this rescue or bait?

chapters.title: Warehouse Nine
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Inside the free port, Marisol maps the syndicate's plan: torch Warehouse Nine, where seized ledgers and a protected witness are stored, and bill it as an electrical accident worth forty million in insurance. She photographs a manifest and hides the chip. Emotional beat: claustrophobic dread as she realizes someone is counting the cameras she avoids.

chapters.title: Follow the Ash
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Using financial forensics, Ansel traces the original fire's insurance payout through shell companies to a custodial firm called Halcyon Trust, finding the same signature accountant on both fires. She is followed leaving the archive. Emotional beat: cold exhilaration curdling into fear when the tail knows her old case names.

chapters.title: Two Sisters, One Alibi
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The sisters meet at a shuttered aquarium; Marisol explains why she stayed dead — witness protection failed her once, so she built her own. Ansel demands they go to the authorities; Marisol shows her the name of the police liaison on Halcyon's payroll. Emotional beat: love rekindled and immediately tested by incompatible definitions of justice.

chapters.title: The Accountant's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel corners the signature accountant, who trades testimony for protection but is found dead hours later, ruled a suicide. His encrypted ledger lands anonymously in Ansel's inbox — someone inside Halcyon is feeding her. Emotional beat: guilt over using a man as a ladder, and the vertigo of an unknown ally.

chapters.title: Counting Cameras
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol identifies her watcher — a port security chief who knew her old face — and realizes the attack has been moved up by six days. Her escape route through the bonded zone closes as her cover frays. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve; she chooses to stay inside rather than run.

chapters.title: What the Records Erase
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel discovers the syndicate's founding crime: Halcyon was built on laundered ransom money, and the Warehouse Nine witness is the surviving bookkeeper of that origin. She plants a mirrored copy of the ledger with three journalists and one honest prosecutor — insurance against her own death. Emotional beat: acceptance that she is now beyond the law she once served.

chapters.title: Accident Weather
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, climax. On the night of the staged fire, Ansel triggers a false alarm audit that freezes the port's bonded zone while Marisol extracts the witness through the flooded sub-basement. The arson team ignites an empty warehouse; the insurance claim collapses on camera. The security chief corners them, and Marisol lets him see her face — a death sentence she accepts. Emotional beat: adrenaline, sacrifice, and the terrible clarity of chosen risk.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, weeks later. Halcyon Trust unravels via the mirrored ledger; the official record credits a whistleblower who does not exist. Marisol, officially still dead, sends one last burner phone with a single saved contact. Ansel takes a new unattributable case — this time one she chose. Emotional beat: bittersweet inheritance; justice delivered off the books, memory kept alive by the sisters alone.
